declared_license.source: README.md 'Licensing' (repository default plus path rows; Notion 'Declared licensing' decision record; AES-003 has no licensing field)

notes: No CLAUDE.md exists in the repository.
Unknown or missing items are counted under summary.unknown; summary.failures lists files that could not be read or carry conflicting notices.
Test coverage is by reference (a test naming the file or module), not line coverage.
Data and report files are not scanned for notices: their text is election content, not file notices.

findings.finding: Four derived data files were not covered by the declared licensing table.
findings.resolution: Owner rule 2026-10-23: files derived from public data take their source's license. Area files: LicenseRef-WA-SOS-PublicData. Alaska crosswalk: new LicenseRef-AK-DOE-PublicData (text drafted in step 2; the Division's terms stay UNKNOWN in it).

findings.finding: 24 files (and every snapshot from Nov 3) are written by the watcher or the report workflow, so hand-added headers or .license sidecars would be lost or missing on the next automated commit.
findings.resolution: Step 2 proposal: license them with REUSE.toml path annotations so new files are covered automatically; give Catalyst-File-IDs to the 44 authored files only. Data and reports stay identified by the SHA-256 recorded in SOURCES.json and analysis.json.

findings.finding: The Nov 3 election adds sources with no LicenseRef yet: Snohomish, Pierce, Kittitas and Chelan counties (results.votewa.gov), the Alaska Division of Elections and the Maine Secretary of State.
findings.resolution: Owner rule 2026-10-23 and the README note on other Washington counties: one LicenseRef per publisher in the King County form, with UNKNOWN where terms are not stated. Drafted in step 2.

findings.finding: The two election LicenseRef texts are at the repository root and list pre-move paths; a REUSE check rooted at election-analysis/ (as for crypto_pipeline) needs the texts in election-analysis/LICENSES/.
findings.resolution: Step 2: move them with git mv into election-analysis/LICENSES/, refresh their Applies-to paths, and add Apache-2.0 and CC-BY-4.0 texts.

findings.finding: This baseline is JSON under docs/engineering/, which the repository-wide *.json rule ignores (as crypto_pipeline F3).
